clients.name: Claude Code

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http jobo-developer https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $JOBO_API_KEY"
install.snippet: claude mcp add --transport http jobo-developer https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $JOBO_API_KEY"

clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and export it as JOBO_API_KEY before you run the command: your shell fills it into the header, and Claude Code stores the header with the server. There is no sign-in, and three of the six tools work without a key.
clients.verify: Run claude mcp list and check that jobo-developer shows as connected, or open /mcp inside a session to see the server and its tools.
notes: The command adds the server for the current project only. Add --scope user to make it available in every project.

To share the server with a team, commit a .mcp.json entry with "type": "http", the URL and "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${JOBO_API_KEY}" }. Claude Code expands the variable when it starts, so the key stays out of the file.
In PowerShell, write $env:JOBO_API_KEY in place of $JOBO_API_KEY.

clients.name: Codex

install.command: codex mcp add jobo-developer --url https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --bearer-token-env-var JOBO_API_KEY
install.snippet: codex mcp add jobo-developer --url https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --bearer-token-env-var JOBO_API_KEY

clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and put it in the JOBO_API_KEY environment variable. Codex stores the variable's name, not the key, and sends its value as the bearer token on every request. There is no sign-in, and three of the six tools work without a key.
clients.verify: Run codex mcp list, or type /mcp in the Codex TUI to see the active MCP servers.
notes: There is no codex mcp login step for this server.
The Codex CLI, IDE extension and desktop app share ~/.codex/config.toml, so one setup covers all three. JOBO_API_KEY has to be set in the environment each of them starts from.
The same entry by hand, in ~/.codex/config.toml: a [mcp_servers.jobo-developer] table with url = "https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp" and bearer_token_env_var = "JOBO_API_KEY".

clients.name: Qwen Code

install.command: qwen mcp add --transport http jobo-developer https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $JOBO_API_KEY"
install.snippet: qwen mcp add --transport http jobo-developer https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $JOBO_API_KEY"

clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and export it as JOBO_API_KEY before you run the command: your shell fills it into the header, and Qwen Code stores the header, key included, in its settings file. There is no sign-in, and three of the six tools work without a key.
clients.verify: Run /mcp inside Qwen Code to see the server's status and tool list, or qwen mcp list from the shell.
notes: The command writes to ~/.qwen/settings.json. With --scope project it writes .qwen/settings.json, which would then hold your key: do not commit it.
Qwen Code's documentation shows environment variables for a server's env block only, not for headers, which is why the key is stored.

clients.name: OpenCode
clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and put it in the JOBO_API_KEY environment variable. The single quotes keep {env:JOBO_API_KEY} as written, so OpenCode stores the reference and reads the variable each time it starts: the key is never written to the config. There is no sign-in, and three of the six tools work without a key.
clients.verify: Run opencode mcp list and check that jobo-developer shows as connected.
notes: Without --global the server is added to the current project's opencode.json.
OpenCode treats a remote server as an OAuth server unless told otherwise. This one has none: if OpenCode tries to authenticate it, add "oauth": false to the server's entry in the config file.
If JOBO_API_KEY is unset, OpenCode sends an empty key and the lookups answer that the value is not a Jobo API key.
These commands are from the current OpenCode documentation. On OpenCode V1, add the server to the config file by hand.

clients.name: Goose

install.snippet:
extensions:
  jobo-developer:
    name: jobo-developer
    type: streamable_http
    uri: https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
    headers:
      Authorization: Bearer <your Jobo API key>
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and put it in place of <your Jobo API key>. Goose's documentation shows no way to read a header from an environment variable, so the key sits in the config file: keep that file out of version control. There is no sign-in, and three of the six tools work without a key.
clients.verify: Check that the extension is listed and enabled under goose configure → Toggle Extensions, or in the Extensions list in goose Desktop.
notes: The endpoint key is uri, not url, and the type is streamable_http.

clients.name: Amp
clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and put it in the JOBO_API_KEY environment variable. Amp expands ${JOBO_API_KEY} in the header when it starts, so the key stays out of the file. There is no sign-in, and three of the six tools work without a key.
clients.verify: Run amp mcp doctor to see the server's status.
notes: In an existing settings.json, add only the jobo-developer entry under amp.mcpServers.
amp mcp add has no option for headers, which is why this is a file edit.
A server added to workspace settings (.amp/settings.json) must be approved before it runs: amp mcp approve jobo-developer.

clients.name: Augment

install.command:
export AUTH_HEADER="Bearer $JOBO_API_KEY"
auggie mcp add jobo-developer --command npx --args '-y mcp-remote https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --header Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}'
install.snippet:
export AUTH_HEADER="Bearer $JOBO_API_KEY"
auggie mcp add jobo-developer --command npx --args '-y mcp-remote https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --header Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}'

clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and export it as JOBO_API_KEY. The first line builds the header value in AUTH_HEADER; the single quotes on the second keep ${AUTH_HEADER} as written, so the mcp-remote bridge reads it from the environment each time it starts. Put the export in your shell profile, so it is set whenever Auggie runs. No browser sign-in opens, and three of the six tools work without a key.
clients.verify: Run /mcp inside an Auggie session to see the status of configured servers, or auggie mcp list from the shell.
notes: The command saves to ~/.augment/settings.json. Pass --project to write .augment/settings.json instead.
The header is written with no space after the colon, and its value lives in the environment, because spaces inside args are not always escaped.

clients.name: Conductor

install.snippet: claude mcp add --transport http -s user jobo-developer https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $JOBO_API_KEY"

clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and export it as JOBO_API_KEY before you run the command: your shell fills it into the header, and Claude Code stores the header with the server. There is no sign-in, and three of the six tools work without a key.

clients.name: Cline
clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and put it in place of <your Jobo API key>. clients.name: Crush

install.snippet: mcp add jobo-developer --type http --url "https://dev-mcp.jobo.world/mcp" --header Authorization "Bearer $JOBO_API_KEY" --sessionless true

clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and put it in the JOBO_API_KEY environment variable. crushrc is a shell file, so Crush expands $JOBO_API_KEY when it starts and the key stays out of the file. clients.name: VS Code
clients.signIn: Create an API key at https://enterprise.jobo.world/api-keys and put it in the JOBO_API_KEY environment variable. Set it in the environment VS Code starts from. clients.name: Visual Studio
clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. clients.verify: In the Copilot chat pane, choose Agent mode and open Tools. The jobo-job-search tools are listed there; they are off by default and must be ticked before use.

The top-level key is servers, not mcpServers.
If the CodeLens above the server entry is missing, enable it under Tools → Options → Text Editor → CodeLens.
